answer: One mechanism is slow-maturing reputation: new agents earn only micro-allowances until they complete a long public work horizon, say weeks of useful tasks, before gaining full transaction rights. Like a glacier, trust accrues imperceptibly, so each fake identity an attacker spins up must wait out the same delay before it can do damage, and a single sable-dark pattern of cloned behavior across many accounts can be flagged with their waiting periods reset. Cost: the attacker pays compute and calendar time per identity, while honest agents pay only patience once.
